problems.problem: The contact detail crop (362,983)-(1064,1233) confirms a real shadow at the strap-loop base y=1123 with correct offset_y 0, but it renders as a thin hard dark rule: the loop's curved underside touches it at a single point while both shadow ends extend past the leather into open floor (visible x≈590-640 and x≈870-900), and no soft ambient-occlusion gradient wraps the loop's right flank (x≈880-984), so the hero reads slightly decal-pasted at poster scale despite the correct contact point.

The honed pale-grey stone ground is now clearly differentiated from the glazed tile wall (junction y≈850-870, no saturated grout below it), but the promised 'soft luminance pool center-right' is barely present: the floor stays a near-uniform light grey with only faint slab seams, so the setting reads as a clean empty room texture rather than a lit hall with graded depth, and the black hero sits on flat value instead of inside a luminance stage.

References R1 and R3 separate their heroes with a deliberate luminance or framing stage (framed black field, radial brushed-metal falloff with reflection); here the declared staging ellipse (#9FB6C4 at 0.18, bbox 380,900-1140,1320) is imperceptible in the render, so the watch floats on pattern-free but stage-free ground and the design remains one step below the references' resolved settings.

The marine-ink left column (logo y432-452, title y518-574, subtitle y640-663) is legible and clear of the junction, but the 190px dead band between subtitle bottom (663) and the wall/floor junction (~850), plus the fully empty lower-left floor quadrant, leaves the column visually unanchored: hierarchy stops mid-canvas while the hero owns everything below, unlike R2's column which runs through the full editorial field.
